nodes.name: Feasibility of a Multimodal Lifestyle Intervention Programme for Patients With Ulcerative Colitis: A Single‐Arm Pilot Study
nodes.venue: JCC Plus
nodes.abstract: Plain Language Summary Lifestyle factors, such as exercise, diet and mental health, have shown promise in improving well‐being in people with ulcerative colitis, a chronic inflammatory condition of the large bowel. However, these factors are usually addressed separately in research. Therefore, we explored whether a 24‐week programme combining exercise, personalised dietary advice and psychological support could be implemented in people with ulcerative colitis. Thirty patients took part in the programme. Most participants remained in the study, and three‐quarters were satisfied with the programme. However, maintaining participation across the different components proved challenging. In particular, adherence to the exercise programme was low, whereas adherence to dietary advice was higher. More than half of the participants were eligible for psychological support, but only a quarter of those started the programme. No unexpected safety concerns were observed. Overall, our findings suggest that patients may be interested in a broad lifestyle approach, but that initial interest does not necessarily translate into sustained participation. Therefore, future programmes should focus on making lifestyle interventions more flexible, practical and tailored to individual people.

nodes.name: Pasture area increases livestock rabies risk in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil: a geospatial analysis of neurological syndrome cases (2020–2024)
nodes.venue: Tropical Animal Health and Production
nodes.abstract: Abstract Animal rabies poses a risk to livestock in Brazil due to transmission by hematophagous bats. The Brazilian sanitary surveillance system mandates rabies testing for any livestock exhibiting signs of neurological syndrome. This geospatial, retrospective, longitudinal, observational study analyzed rabies test results for 204 cattle and 56 horses presenting with neurological syndrome in Rio de Janeiro State, Brazil, from 2020 to 2024. We calculated correlations and linear models between rabies results and municipal land-use types, as well the population of herbivores. Most neurological syndrome cases and positive rabies results occurred in cattle. The final linear model for the number of neurological syndrome cases and positive rabies results incorporated pasture area, shrub area and cattle population. Pasture area was positively correlated with higher numbers ( p = 0.011 and p = 0.005, respectively). Larger shrub area was associated with fewer neurological syndrome reports and fewer positive results ( p = 0.009 and p = 0.010, respectively). Greater cattle population showed a negative association with neurological syndrome notifications and positive detections ( p = 0.085 and p = 0.046, respectively).A higher proportion of positive rabies tests was associated with larger pasture areas ( p = 0.019) and with lower equine populations ( p = 0.115). These findings indicate that the lower animal diversity in pasture areas provides few alternative feeding options for Desmodus rotundus besides livestock, leading to more neurological syndrome cases and animal rabies infections. A larger shrub area offer feed alternatives other than cattle to the bats and a larger cattle population dilutes the frequency of bat meals across individuals, reducing both neurological syndrome notifications and positive rabies detections.

nodes.name: Dual-tapered graded-index two-mode fiber and peak-detection improvement algorithm for refractive index sensing
nodes.venue: Applied Optics
nodes.abstract: Dual tapers based on a graded-index (GI) two-mode (TM) fiber are proposed for refractive index (RI) sensing in this work. Sensitivity of 1433.94 nm/RIU with R 2 =0.98 is achieved using the direct peak-finding method, where the sensitivity enhancement originated from two guided modes and corresponding two sets of excited cladding modes. To improve wavelength demodulation accuracy, spatial frequency concentration algorithm is presented to filter out the influence of optical intensity fluctuations and mode noise via a bandpass filter, and yielding the sensing sensitivity 1669.61 nm/RIU and R 2 =0.9699 after data processing. Furthermore, empirical mode decomposition (EMD) is utilized to decompose transmission spectra according to their noise features. By calculating correlation coefficients between each intrinsic mode function and the raw spectrum, noise components are eliminated to smooth the spectra. The EMD-processed spectra produce the sensing sensitivity of 1458.52 nm/RIU with R 2 =0.9930 through peak-finding again. Experimental results demonstrate that the GI two-mode fiber enhances the sensing sensitivity of tapered fiber sensors, while the EMD algorithm improves the sensing accuracy. The results in this work could provide technical support for the practical sensing applications of tapered fiber sensors.

nodes.name: Enhance EV station charge and discharge based on deep learning forecasting method incorporating renewable energy sources and multi-objective optimization algorithm
nodes.venue: International Journal of Renewable Energy Development
nodes.abstract: As electric vehicle charging station operations become more common, proper coordination of energy management is necessary to avoid high operational costs and carbon emissions caused by electric vehicle charging requirements, intermittent renewable sources, and fluctuating electricity rates. In this research, a forecast-based optimization methodology is created with the objective of optimizing the charge-discharge management of a renewable-powered electric vehicle charging station system involving photovoltaic generation, wind generation, fuel cells, electric vehicles, and stationary batteries. First, a recurrent neural network is used to predict relevant time series data, such as photovoltaic energy, wind energy, electric vehicle load demand, fuel cell energy production, and electric vehicle energy consumption. These forecasted data are then applied to a bi-objective energy management optimization problem, which is solved using NSGA-II. The objective is to minimize operating cost and emissions while considering power balance, grid energy exchange, and other operational constraints associated with the fuel cell, battery storage system, and electric vehicles. In this study, two scenarios are examined using one month of hourly data; Scenario 1 does not use stationary batteries, whereas Scenario 2 uses them. The forecasting results show robust predictions, with one-hour-ahead values ranging from 0.9162 to 0.9708. The optimization results show that Scenario 2 provides better energy shifting and peak-period support through battery charging and discharging management. Compared with Scenario 1, the operating cost is reduced from $171,833.86 to $160,388.44, and emissions are decreased from 13,485.48 kg to 12,892.23 kg, leading to 6.7% and 4.4% reductions, respectively.

nodes.name: International Journal of Renewable Energy Development
A Semi‐Interpretable Multimodal Model Combining Electronic Health Records and Chest X‐Rays for <scp>COVID</scp> ‐19‐Related Death Prediction
nodes.venue: Expert Systems
nodes.abstract: ABSTRACT Purpose Prognostic models can benefit from integrating heterogeneous data sources. While deep learning‐based multimodal models often improve predictive performance, their limited interpretability remains a barrier to clinical adoption. Moreover, achieving robust generalization with such models typically requires large and diverse datasets, which are not always available in clinical research. This study evaluated whether a late fusion model combining traditional statistical approaches with deep learning models could rival deep learning‐only multimodal models while preserving interpretability to support clinical use. Methods We conducted a retrospective single‐center cohort study of 965 hospitalized patients with laboratory‐confirmed SARS‐CoV‐2 infection who underwent frontal chest X‐ray imaging during hospitalization between March 2020 and January 2022. Of these, 64 (6.6%) died. Structured clinical data and chest X‐ray images were used to predict COVID‐19‐related death. We developed unimodal baseline models and two multimodal approaches: a deep learning‐based joint fusion model and a late fusion model leveraging logistic regression to combine predictions from the best‐performing models for every data modality. Given the limited sample size and class imbalance, performance was evaluated using repeated five‐fold cross validation. Results The late fusion model achieved the best overall performance, with the highest median test AUPRC of 0.363 (IQR 0.271–0.384) across cross validation folds, outperforming unimodal baselines based on structured clinical data or images alone. The late fusion model also outperformed the joint fusion model, achieving, respectively, a 3.1% and 3.6% relative improvement in AUPRC and Brier score on pooled out‐of‐sample predictions and yielding the highest balanced F1‐score. Moreover, it preserved partial interpretability by linking predictions to clinically meaningful variables such as age and comorbidities and enabling image‐based predictions to be traced back to radiographic abnormalities. Conclusions Late fusion models integrating statistical models for clinical data with deep learning for image classification can enhance prognostic performance over unimodal models without fully sacrificing interpretability. In settings with limited data, they may also outperform deep learning‐based joint fusion models. These findings support late fusion as a promising strategy that warrants prospective evaluation and external validation before clinical implementation.

nodes.name: Hyperspectral Imaging-Based Adulteration Detection of Edible Oil using Optimized Machine Learning Models
nodes.venue: Food Analytical Methods
nodes.abstract: Abstract Oil adulteration poses a significant risk to public health and compromises food quality and authenticity, necessitating reliable and rapid detection methods. This study proposes a non-destructive method for detecting edible oil adulteration using hyperspectral imaging integrated with spectral feature optimization and machine learning techniques. A total of 480 samples, comprising pure oils (tea tree, rose, turmeric, and rosehip oil) and adulterated variants (orange, vitamin E, lemon, and garlic oil), were analyzed using a Specim FX10 camera system. The Savitzky–Golay filter was used to preprocess spectral data, remove noise, and improve spectral smoothness. The spectral features were then optimized and used to train and test various machine learning models, such as Linear Discriminant Analysis, CatBoost, Gradient Boosting Machine, and Extreme Gradient Boosting Machine. The best-performing model among the evaluated models was the Extreme Gradient Boosting Machine, with 99.98% training accuracy, 98.2% testing and validation accuracy, high precision, recall, F1-score, and balanced accuracy (98.3%), Jaccard Index (96.7%), and low log loss (5%) and Hamming loss (2%). The experimental results point to the usefulness of the proposed method in providing accurate, fast, and non-invasive oil adulteration detection. This study indicates the possibility of using hyperspectral imaging with optimized machine learning algorithms to achieve high food quality measurements and real-time applications in the industrial sector of food safety and quality control.

nodes.name: Toward Individualized Digital Twins for Aero-Engines: A Physics-Informed Framework With Fleet-Individual Cross-Attention and Feature Transfer
nodes.venue: Journal of Engineering for Gas Turbines and Power
nodes.abstract: Abstract Digital twin (DT) technology has become a cornerstone for cyber-physical aero-engine systems, enabling full lifecycle digital replication and intelligent management. To address challenges of model adaptability and generalization under restricted access to fleet data conditions, this article proposes a physics-informed DT modeling framework integrating fleet feature transfer and a fleet-individual cross-attention fusion mechanism. The framework is composed of three main components: (1) a physics-embedded network, where a long short-term memory network captures temporal component dynamics, coupled with a multicomponent attention module to model intercomponent interactions; (2) a fleet-individual cross-attention module designed to extract interactive features between individual engines and the entire fleet; and (3) a pretraining and fine-tuning strategy that transfers generalized knowledge from fleet-level models to individual engines, enabling fast deployment without relying on large-scale historical data. Validation on thrust and exhaust gas temperature (EGT) prediction demonstrates superior accuracy and robustness, achieving the lowest mean absolute percentage errors (MAPEs) of 0.23% for thrust and 2.47% for EGT. Compared with baselines (a general fleet model and individual models without fleet features), the proposed approach reduces average MAPE by 47.80–75.49% (thrust) and 4.43–15.91% (EGT), improving both precision and stability. This framework enhances the scalability and digital management efficiency of aero-engine DT systems.

nodes.name: Journal of Engineering for Gas Turbines and Power
Beyond the visible lesion: mycotoxin attenuation and spatial heterogeneity in maize cobs
nodes.venue: Mycotoxin Research
nodes.abstract: Abstract Visible mould is widely used as a practical sorting cue in maize, but it remains unclear whether the visible lesion marks the boundary of mycotoxin contamination within an intact cob. This study examined mycotoxin attenuation, spatial heterogeneity, and co-occurrence in visibly mouldy white maize cobs, using measured distances from the visible mould margin. Cobs with visible mould ( n = 35) were sampled for the study. For each cob, the visible mould margin was coded as 0 mm, and adjacent sections were collected at the 50% and 75% points along the measured distance from the lesion boundary to the distal cob tip, resulting in 98 cob-section observations. Mycotoxins, FUMs (FB1, FB2, FB3), deoxynivalenol (DON), zearalenone (ZEA), nivalenol (NIV) and AF (AFB1) were quantified by liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry. Samples with no detectable levels of mycotoxins were replaced with zero, and total FUMs were calculated (FB1 + FB2 + FB3). The visible mould margin accounted for the largest share of the measured toxin burden, accounting for 84.4% of total FUM, 89.4% of DON, 77.8% of ZEA, and 92.2% of NIV. Adjacent sections retained measurable residual mycotoxins, including 15.6% of total FUM, 10.6% of DON, 22.2% of ZEA, and 7.8% of NIV. In full-distance models, DON, ZEA, and NIV declined significantly with distance, whereas total FUM did not show significant monotonic attenuation. The AFB1 was detected in only three cob sections; these detections co-occurred with Fusarium -associated toxins. Co-occurrence analysis showed that adjacent sections frequently remained positive for multiple Fusarium -associated toxin groups, with the FUM + DON + ZEA profile persisting across measured-distance bands. These findings show that visible mould is a useful warning signal but not a reliable toxicological boundary. The results support cob-level rejection or segregation of visibly mouldy cobs before shelling, rather than lesion-level trimming, as a more defensible food-safety control measure.

nodes.name: Breaking GUI Agent Actions: Realistic Adversarial Attacks on Multimodal LLMs
nodes.venue: ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications, and Applications
nodes.abstract: Recent progress in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) has enabled GUI agents that interpret interface screenshots and execute natural-language instructions. However, their increasing role in human–computer interaction raises security concerns. Existing work shows that MLLMs are highly sensitive to interface perturbations, yet most attacks assume unrealistic capabilities such as direct access to model-ready inputs. In real deployments, attackers cannot control the screenshot pipeline or the non-differentiable preprocessing operations preceding inference, rendering many prior attacks ineffective. We introduce Realistic Adversarial Attack (RAA) framework that models the complete screenshot-to-prediction pipeline. To address gradient blockage from non-differentiable preprocessing (e.g., resizing and quantization), we develop a dual-branch differentiable preprocessing module that restores gradient flow while remaining faithful to the actual inference path. To improve robustness against query phrasing changes, we further incorporate a task-level semantic variation mechanism that jointly optimizes over paraphrased task variants. Experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B-Instruct and GUI-Owl-7B show that RAA consistently outperforms prior attacks, improving attack success rates by an average of 30% under localized perturbations and a 10.7% under global perturbations, while maintaining strong effectiveness against standard defenses such as resizing, compression, and noise. Ablation studies highlight the roles of perturbation region and semantic diversity. Our framework establishes a practical threat model for GUI agents and offers a foundation for future robustness and security research.

nodes.name: ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications, and Applications
CoBiDiff: anatomy-aware bidirectional diffusion for left atrium cross-modal augmentation
nodes.venue: Measurement Science and Technology
nodes.abstract: Abstract Accurate delineation of the left atrium (LA) from cardiac magnetic resonance (MR) and computed tomography (CT) images plays an important role in atrial fibrillation assessment and treatment planning. However, the limited availability of expert-annotated cardiac datasets restricts the robustness and generalizability of deep learning–based segmentation models, particularly in cross-modal scenarios. To overcome this limitation, we propose CoBiDiff, a collaborative bidirectional diffusion framework that explicitly incorporates anatomical constraints into unpaired cross-modal cardiac image augmentation. The framework is developed using unpaired CT and MR volumes from the MICCAI 2017 multi-modality whole heart segmentation (MM-WHS) challenge dataset, focusing specifically on the LA region. A shared diffusion backbone is employed to jointly model both imaging modalities, while signed distance functions (SDFs) are incorporated as structural representations to provide anatomical guidance during generation. To reduce the influence of artificial CT field-of-view boundaries, boundary regions are suppressed through noise replacement and gradient smoothing strategies. In addition, a soft spatial extent loss is introduced to maintain anatomically plausible foreground spatial extents during synthesis. An SDF dropout strategy is further introduced during training to strengthen image-conditioned anatomical inference and improve anatomical coherence. Experimental results indicate that the proposed framework generates LA images with improved structural consistency across modalities. The proposed method achieved Dice coefficients of 86.53% and 95.04%, and average symmetric surface distances of 1.511 mm and 0.623 mm for CT-to-MR and MR-to-CT augmentation, respectively, on the MM-WHS 2017 dataset. CoBiDiff provides a practical framework for expanding limited cardiac imaging datasets without requiring paired cross-modal images. By combining diffusion-based synthesis with anatomy-aware constraints, CoBiDiff improves the downstream utility of generated samples for cardiac segmentation. The full implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/PencilSC/CoBiDiff to support reproducible and open research.

nodes.name: A Physics‐Informed Two‐Stage Retrieval Method for EMIT Remote Sensing Methane Plumes
nodes.venue: Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres
nodes.abstract: Abstract Hyperspectral satellite missions, particularly EMIT, have revolutionized methane point source monitoring. However, current operational retrieval pipelines typically rely on physically‐based matched filters followed by labor‐intensive manual verification to mitigate high false alarm rates caused by complex background interference. This dependence on human intervention restricts the scalability and efficiency required for rapid, automated global monitoring. To address these limitations, this paper proposes Plume‐Net, a novel Physics‐Informed Guided Two‐Stage Retrieval Method. Unlike conventional approaches, Plume‐Net decouples the task into a “global existence classification” stage and a “local pixel‐level regression” stage to maximize reliability without human‐in‐the‐loop. The core innovation lies in the integration of physical priors with deep learning: In the first stage, a Physics‐Informed Spectral Gating (PISG) module explicitly injects methane spectral absorption knowledge into the network, dynamically recalibrating channel weights to suppress background noise. In the second stage, to overcome the difficulties of regressing sparse, long‐tail plume distributions, we propose a Plume‐Focused Sampling Strategy and an Intensity‐Aware Pixel‐Level Weighted Loss function, forcing the network to prioritize rare but critical high‐concentration signals. Evaluated on real‐world EMIT observations, Plume‐Net achieves an ROC‐AUC of 0.961 in detection and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 33.33 ppm·m in quantification. By significantly reducing false positives while maintaining high precision, this method offers a robust, fully automated alternative to current semi‐manual retrieval workflows.

nodes.name: UCRG: Reliability-Gated Multi-Source Prediction Integration for Forest Point Cloud Semantic Segmentation Across Sensing Platforms
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) scanning and mobile laser scanning provide detailed three-dimensional observations for forest inventory and structural monitoring for which point-wise separation of ground, understory, woody components, and foliage is fundamental. Modern segmentation pipelines can produce multiple predictions from different feature configurations, training objectives, random seeds, or network architectures. However, equal and fixed-weight fusion implicitly assume stable source quality, although the relative reliability of these predictions can vary across semantic classes and sensing conditions, leading to error propagation and negative transfer. We therefore formulate multi-source prediction integration as a calibration-supported class-wise reliability decision problem and propose the unified class-wise reliability gate (UCRG). The UCRG measures global and class-wise source reliability from labeled calibration data, uses shrinkage to stabilize class-specific estimates when labels are scarce, and conditionally performs soft fusion or hard source selection according to the reliability gap. An optional calibration-guided confusion-pair refiner further targets residual ambiguity between semantically similar classes. All the reliability estimation and parameter selection processes are performed without query labels. Experiments on FOR-instance, EvoMLS, and Lin3D cover UAV and mobile laser scanning together with cross-dataset transfer. Using one shared parameterization across the three primary protocols, the UCRG obtains 70.68% mIoU and records two negative-transfer episodes across the six evaluated episodes compared with six for fixed-weight fusion. When the gate parameters are selected solely from the available calibration support in each deployment, the UCRG reaches 59.20% mean mIoU in the PTv3-augmented Lin3D candidate pool. These results show that reliability-guided decisions can exploit class-dependent complementarity across heterogeneous frozen predictors and sensing conditions.

nodes.name: Trackerless Augmented Reality Navigation for Robotic Partial Nephrectomy using Simultaneous Localization and Mapping
nodes.abstract: Abstract Purpose. To evaluate the performance of a novel trackerless surgical navigation system for partial nephrectomy using 3D laparoscopy integrated with the simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) algorithm. Materials and Methods. Patients undergoing robotic partial nephrectomy were retrospectively analyzed. From the preoperative CT/MR images, three-dimensional (3D) models of the kidney, tumor, and vasculature were generated using a deep learning-based approach. A calibrated stereo laparoscope acquired stereo video, which was processed using the SLAM algorithm to reconstruct high-fidelity 3D surface models of the kidney. This reconstruction was registered to the preoperative kidney model using anatomical landmarks and surface-based alignment. Augmented overlays of anatomy, including the tumor, were projected onto the surgical view. Accuracy was assessed using surface target registration error (STRE), landmark registration error (LRE), and localization error. A multi-institutional surgeon survey evaluated the trackerless navigation system using 10 representative cases. Results. Twenty patients undergoing robotic partial nephrectomy were analyzed. Dense 3D surface reconstruction and laparoscope calibration were successful in all cases. Mean (SD; range) STRE, LRE, and localization errors were 1.47 (0.5; 0.6–2.5) mm, 4.3 (1.6; 1.1–6.5) mm, and 2.6 (1.2; 0.7–5.2) mm, respectively. Nine surgeons highly rated the 3D and 2D overlays (3.99 and 4.41/5). Reported cognitive load was moderate (2.38), with high scores for anatomical accuracy (4.44), trust in the overlay for intraoperative decision-making (3.89), and likelihood of adoption (4.56) on a 5-point scale. Conclusions. A trackerless SLAM-based navigation system, evaluated retrospectively on recorded operative video, demonstrates the feasibility of accurate augmented visualization during partial nephrectomy.

nodes.name: Shapley-guided token pruning for real-time remote sensing scene classification on edge devices
nodes.venue: Scientific Reports
nodes.abstract: Abstract Vision Transformers (ViTs) excel at remote sensing scene classification, but the quadratic cost of self-attention hinders real-time inference on edge platforms such as on-board satellite and UAV payloads. Token pruning accelerates ViTs, yet mainstream methods rank tokens by attention scores, whose reliability is contested, so aggressive pruning may discard predictively important patches. We instead adopt the axiomatically grounded Shapley contribution as the pruning criterion. To keep its exponential cost out of inference, Shapley values are estimated offline as supervision, and a lightweight head (about 0.10 M parameters) is trained through ranking distillation to reproduce their ranking, so the deployed path performs no Shapley computation; pruning is hierarchical (layers 4/7/10) with a calibrated early-exit recalibrated after pruning. On NWPU-RESISC45 (DeiT-S backbone), the criterion learned by this head follows the offline Shapley ranking more faithfully than attention does (Spearman rho = 0.641 vs. 0.401), with a higher Insertion AUC and a lower Deletion AUC. On a Jetson Orin Nano with TensorRT, latency and per-image energy fall by 24.18% and 32.27% versus the unpruned model. Accuracy at 0.7 retention is 93.04%, 0.53% points above attention pruning; however, with only three paired seeds this comparison is marginal (paired t-test, p = 0.067), and an observed-effect diagnostic power calculation gives only 0.51 at alpha = 0.05. Accordingly, no statistically decisive accuracy improvement is claimed. The contribution is therefore framed as a more faithful pruning criterion and a favourable accuracy-latency trade-off under a single-backbone, single-remote-sensing-benchmark setting, rather than as a general accuracy advantage.

nodes.name: Sensor-Based Monitoring and Control of Precision Seed Metering Systems in Digital Agriculture
nodes.venue: Agronomy
nodes.abstract: Precision seed metering has evolved from mechanically optimized devices to sensor-based, digitally connected systems. However, research remains fragmented across metering mechanisms, sensing, data processing, communication, and control. This review examined monitoring and closed-loop control throughout the seed-delivery process, from pickup and release to tube passage, furrow placement, and crop emergence. This structured review synthesized 49 primary studies identified through Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection, with supplementary searching using Google Scholar and literature coverage through 1 September 2026. Optical and photoelectric sensors provide the most direct evidence for seed-passage detection, whereas encoders, pressure, vacuum, motor-current, and vibration measurements primarily indicate machine or actuator conditions. Machine vision provides spatial information and can support independent reference measurements, but requires suitable imaging conditions and computational resources. Capacitive, acoustic, impact-based, and hybrid approaches remain less extensively validated. Reported performance cannot be directly compared across studies due to differences in seed characteristics, mechanisms, operating speeds, event definitions, disturbances, and reference methods. Most studies demonstrate monitoring, alarms, or open-loop optimization rather than complete sensor-to-actuator correction. An engineering framework is therefore proposed to connect measurement targets, evidence maturity, latency, actuator authority, and independent verification. Future research should prioritize standardized testing, disturbance robustness, synchronized multi-row field validation, and measured end-to-end delay. Transparent reporting of correction accuracy, stability, cost, power demand, and interoperability is also required to support deployment and defensible assessment of closed-loop seeding systems.

nodes.name: Satellite Image Super-resolution Using Diffusion Based Approach
nodes.venue: Book of Abstracts of 10th DeKUT International Conference on Science, Technology, Innovation and Entrepreneurship (STIE 2026)
nodes.abstract: The trade-off between spatial and temporal resolution in satellite imagery limits the use of available data for fine-scale Earth observation. Although Sentinel-2 provides frequent coverage, its 10 m spatial resolution can be insufficient for agricultural monitoring and environmental assessment. This study investigates a pixel-space diffusion-based super-resolution approach using Super-Resolution via Iterative Refinement (SR3) to generate 2.5 m spatial-resolution estimates from 10 m Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery. Unlike latent diffusion approaches, SR3 performs diffusion and denoising in image pixel space without transforming imagery into a latent representation. The model was trained using the SEN2NAIP dataset and evaluated in Cuyama Valley, Santa Barbara County, California, USA, using NAIP imagery, and through zero-shot deployment in Kenya using PlanetScope as a reference. The generated 2.5 m products represent spatially enhanced estimates rather than direct observations of 2.5 m information. Performance was assessed using mean squared error (MSE), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index (SSIM), and edge preservation index (EPI), with bicubic interpolation and OpenSR, a latent-space diffusion model, as baselines. In Cuyama Valley, SR3 improved SSIM from 0.246 to 0.389 and PSNR from 8.2 to 14.0 dB while reducing MSE from 0.1515 to 0.0304 compared with bicubic interpolation. SR3 also outperformed OpenSR, achieving SSIM of 0.384 and PSNR of 14.0 dB compared with 0.249 and 8.19 dB, respectively. In the zero-shot Kenyan evaluation, bicubic interpolation produced lower MSE, higher PSNR, and higher SSIM than both diffusion models at Kieni Forest and Dedan Kimathi University of Technology, while SR3 demonstrated competitive edge preservation. These findings show that pixel-space diffusion can enhance Sentinel-2 spatial detail within the training domain, while zero-shot performance remains sensitive to cross-sensor and geographic differences. The imagery has potential for precision agriculture, vegetation monitoring, environmental assessment, land-cover mapping, and coastal and marine science, where enhanced spatial detail can complement Sentinel-2’s temporal coverage.

nodes.name: Book of Abstracts of 10th DeKUT International Conference on Science, Technology, Innovation and Entrepreneurship (STIE 2026)
RoPE-T: Rotary Position Embedding for Enhanced Temporal Modeling in Video-Based Human Action Recognition
nodes.venue: Electronics
nodes.abstract: Human action recognition requires modeling both spatial information and temporal relationships across video frames. While Transformer encoders are effective for capturing long-range dependencies, standard self-attention mechanisms do not inherently encode the sequential order of input tokens. To address this limitation, we introduce RoPE-T, a RoPE-enhanced temporal Transformer framework for video-based human action recognition. Our approach employs a pretrained EfficientNetV2B0 as a lightweight spatial feature extractor, followed by a temporal Transformer encoder. We apply Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) directly to the query and key projections within the self-attention module, allowing relative temporal position information to influence the attention scores without modifying the spatial backbone. We also investigate the effect of the rotary base parameter on action recognition performance, showing that its impact varies across datasets and Transformer configurations. Evaluations on the UCF101 and HMDB51 datasets show improvements over our baseline model under identical architectural and training settings, increasing accuracy from 91.51% to 91.59% on UCF101 and from 74.51% to 75.10% on HMDB51. After tuning, the proposed RoPE-T model achieves accuracies of 91.91% on UCF101 and 78.82% on HMDB51, outperforming several previously published action recognition methods on both benchmarks. These results indicate that RoPE is a viable alternative for incorporating relative temporal positional information into CNN–Transformer models for human action recognition.

nodes.name: Recovery in Place: A Multimodal Pilot Study of Neighborhood Context, Life-Space, and Social and Physical Functioning After Lower-Limb Fracture Surgery
nodes.abstract: Abstract Background Older adults returning home after lower-limb fracture surgery or hip replacement recover within heterogeneous social and spatial contexts, yet neighborhood conditions are rarely integrated into post-discharge monitoring. Guided by the capability approach and the life-space concept, this study examined recovery as a situated process shaped by residential context, activity space, and changing social and physical function after discharge. Methods Eighteen community-dwelling older adults completed eight weeks of monitoring, contributing 1,008 person-days of multimodal sensor data and repeated biweekly clinical assessments. Clinical measures included the Social Isolation Scale, Oxford Hip Score, Oxford Knee Score, Timed Up and Go test, and 30-second chair-stand test. Residential and visited locations were linked to amenity, crime, and Canadian census-derived socioeconomic data. Generalized estimating equations tested associations between socio-spatial exposures and the Social Isolation Scale, Oxford Hip Score, and Oxford Knee Score. Predictive models compared sensor-only, socio-spatial-only, and combined feature sets for all clinical outcomes under random-shuffled and cross-person validation. Results Neighborhood material disadvantage was associated with lower social interaction in both residential and activity-space analyses. More location transitions per day were associated with higher social interaction after correction for multiple testing, while other location-derived mobility measures showed exploratory associations. Activity-space exposure to libraries and food establishments was associated with better hip function after correction for multiple testing, whereas similar amenity associations were not observed around the residence. Predictive performance varied by model, outcome, and validation setting. Prediction errors were generally higher under cross-person validation, and socio-spatial features improved prediction for some outcomes and models but not others. Conclusions These preliminary findings suggest that post-discharge recovery is shaped by the interaction between changing bodily capacity and the social and spatial environments that become accessible during recovery. Integrating residential and activity-space context may improve interpretation of remote-monitoring data, but larger longitudinal studies are required before clinical application.

nodes.name: Recontextualizing Netanyahu’s 2023 UN General Assembly Address: A Multimodal Critical Discourse Analysis of the Speech and Six English-Language News Reports
nodes.abstract: Abstract This article examines how Benjamin Netanyahu’s address to the 78th Session of the United Nations General Assembly, delivered on 22 September 2023, was recontextualized in six English-language news reports published during 22–23 September news cycle. Addressing media's role in shaping public understanding of armed conflict and peaceful society, it combines Van Leeuwen’s framework of social actor representation and legitimation with framing and source-to-news recontextualization, while treating verbal, visual-spatial, embodied-performative, and journalistic anchoring resources as analytically distinct but related. The corpus consists of the official audiovisual record, the released speech transcript, and reports from Al Jazeera, Fox News, Reuters, the Associated Press, The Times of Israel, and The Jerusalem Post. The comparison shows an uneven distribution of agency and authority. Israel is largely activated as an agent of regional transformation; American and Saudi leaders are individualized as enabling authorities; Palestinians are mostly collectivized and positioned as conditional participants or possible impediments; and Iran is constructed as the principal antagonist. The paired maps add a visual trajectory from regional isolation to connectivity, but they do not politically differentiate the West Bank and Gaza within the highlighted territorial field. Across the six reports, divergent meanings “rise less from wholly different facts than from differences in selection, quotation, contextual addition, source hierarchy, and resemiotization. Three recurrent patterns capture these shifts: preservation, qualification, and reversal. The article therefore offers a transparent small-case account of how one diplomatic performance acquired competing meanings as it moved through its first cycle of news reporting.

nodes.name: Prediction-Constrained Multimodal Temporal Fusion of Satellite Microwave and Infrared Observations for Continuous Snow Temperature Profile Estimation
nodes.venue: Applied Sciences
nodes.abstract: Snow temperature profiles are important for characterizing snowpack thermal state and vertical heat transfer, but continuous estimation is limited by sparse in situ observations and discrete satellite overpasses. This study proposes a prediction-constrained multimodal temporal fusion method combining continuous deep-learning prediction with satellite microwave–infrared updates. The Weather-Forced Residual LSTM with Persistence Fallback (WFRL-P) generates an hourly multi-depth prediction background from historical snow temperatures and meteorological forcing. Snow temperature profiles are then conjointly retrieved from AMSR2 microwave and MODIS infrared brightness temperatures, and valid retrieval–prediction differences are transformed into depth-dependent, magnitude-limited updates and causally propagated for up to 6 h. Independent evaluation at Dome C during 2020–2021 produced hourly estimates at 12 depths from 5 to 1000 cm, with an all-depth bias of −0.1263 K, MAE of 0.3657 K, RMSE of 0.8218 K, and R2 of 0.9880. At most comparable depths, the estimation errors were lower than those reported in previous Antarctic snow temperature remote-sensing studies. Multimodal fusion further reduced the all-depth MAE of the fixed lead-24 prediction background by 3.32%, with a 5.14% improvement at matched satellite-overpass samples. The results demonstrate that satellite microwave and infrared observations can provide effective incremental constraints while maintaining the overall accuracy of the continuous prediction background, offering a feasible approach for the temporal fusion of discrete satellite observations and continuous snow temperature predictions.

nodes.name: Predicting the Spatial Distribution and Regional Averages of Soil Heavy Metals Based on Stratification
nodes.venue: Journal of Resources and Ecology
nodes.abstract: The significant spatial stratified heterogeneity of soil heavy metal concentrations is a critical characteristic, and effectively capturing this feature can improve the accuracy of spatial interpolation and the reliability of regional mean estimations. This study used 412 soil sampling points in Shunyi District, Beijing, to predict the spatial distribution and regional means of soil heavy metals using a supervised learning-based stratified random forest ordinary Kriging (SRFOK) model. Spatial stratification information of soil heavy metals was extracted via supervised learning and incorporated into the spatial interpolation process. In addition, 21 environmental factors were integrated to enhance the model's ability to characterize spatial heterogeneity. The spatial distributions of the three soil heavy metals cadmium (Cd), chromium (Cr), and copper (Cu) were predicted, and their regional means were estimated. The performance of the SRFOK model was compared with those of ordinary Kriging (OK) and random forest ordinary Kriging (RFOK). Regional mean concentrations were calculated based on the interpolation results and further assessed using the sandwich estimator as a reference. The results demonstrated that the SRFOK model achieved the best prediction performance for all three heavy metals, with coefficients of determination (R2) of 0.619 (Cd), 0.635 (Cr), and 0.498 (Cu), representing improvements of 26% to 100% compared to the OK and RFOK models, as well as the lowest root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE). Regional means obtained from the different models were generally consistent, and the overall concentrations of Cd, Cr, and Cu in the study area were higher than their background values in Beijing. The findings indicate that incorporating supervised learning-based stratification information into spatial interpolation enhances both the accuracy of spatial interpolation and the stability of regional mean estimation for soil heavy metals, so it is an effective approach for high-precision mapping and regional pollution risk assessment.

nodes.name: Precision-Oriented Sensing and Multimodal Visuo-Haptic Interaction for Fine Manipulation in Biomedical Engineering and Assistive Applications
nodes.venue: Sensors
nodes.abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) simulations in high-stake domains, such as surgical training or robotic teleoperation, require both high visual fidelity and accurate force feedback to facilitate embodied cognition and prevent errors. However, current commercial haptic devices impose a critical trade-off: while they provide force feedback, their embedded sensors are known to be prone to latency, hysteresis, and tracking noise, which may limit the precise finger flexion tracking necessary for fine manual dexterity. Conversely, data gloves designed specifically for precise finger tracking offer finer input granularity but lack active force feedback capabilities. To address these limitations, we introduce a hybrid architecture that simultaneously deploys precision-oriented data gloves and haptic gloves, presenting a proof-of-concept user study to examine the performance benefits and trade-offs of combining precision-oriented tracking with direct haptic feedback during the fine manipulation of delicate virtual objects. From our findings, we derive insights into optimizing multimodal visuo-haptic interaction for future biomedical and assistive environments.

nodes.name: Portable Multimodal Screening of Patchouli Oil Using Gravimetric–Ultrasonic Density Measurement and Smartphone Image Colorimetry
nodes.abstract: Abstract A portable measurement platform was developed for preliminary screening of patchouli-oil samples by combining gravimetric–ultrasonic density estimation, smartphone-based RGB/HSL image acquisition, temperature monitoring using a W1209 controller, and Internet of Things data transmission. Density measurements were compared with reference values for 16 sample compositions comprising pure Gayo Lues and Aceh Besar patchouli oils, mixtures with palm oil or kerosene, and adulterant controls. Based on the 16 tabulated paired central values, the mean signed difference (instrument minus reference) was + 0.00075 g cm⁻³, the mean absolute error was 0.006875 g cm⁻³, the root-mean-square error was 0.006946 g cm⁻³, and the coefficient of determination for linear regression was R² = 0.9749. The mean absolute percentage error was 0.796%. An exploratory paired t-test yielded t(15) = 0.421, p = 0.680; this non-significant result is not interpreted as proof of method equivalence. Because replicate-level readings, calibration records, and the definition of the reported ± terms were not supplied, these statistics characterize the tabulated central values rather than full metrological performance. The prototype is therefore presented as a preliminary screening platform, not a substitute for standardized laboratory authentication.

nodes.name: Pixel-Wise Prediction of Glioblastoma Recurrence Using Mid-Treatment MRI and Deep Learning
nodes.venue: Cancers
nodes.abstract: Introduction: Glioblastoma (GBM) commonly recurs close to the original gross tumor volume (GTV), suggesting treatment-resistant subregions may be present before radiologically visible progression. This study investigated whether deep learning on apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps could generate pixel-wise probability maps of treatment-resistant regions within the GTV. Methods: The training/validation set included images of 64 in-house patients after radiation fraction 10 (Fx10) and 40 external patients before treatment used as an auxiliary cross-domain training cohort; the held-out test set included 16 in-house Fx10 patients. Resistant regions were defined as the overlap between the GTV from scans acquired at radiation fraction 10 and subsequent recurrence after finishing treatment. Models were trained on 2D GTV-cropped slices with patient-level separation to prevent data leakage. Single- and multimodal MRI inputs were compared, and ADC-based models (including baseline UNet, pretrained ResNet34, BiomedCLIP-assisted UNet, and a BLIP image-text UNet) were later evaluated. Performance was evaluated using conventional metrics, including ROC AUC, PR AUC, F1-score, recall, specificity, and precision. Results: ADC was the most informative single modality, achieving 69% and 80% for Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC)- and Precision-Recall (PR)-Area Under the Curve (AUC), respectively. In the ADC-based architecture comparison, no model was consistently superior across all metrics. The baseline UNet achieved the highest accuracy, F1-score, and recall, whereas pretrained ResNet34 and BLIP-assisted models showed slightly higher ROC AUC than the baseline UNet (both 70%). Error analysis showed that performance decreased substantially for small or sparse resistant regions, and false-negative errors were enriched near resistant-region and GTV boundaries. Conclusions: ADC-based deep learning showed feasibility for pixel-wise spatial mapping of treatment-resistant glioblastoma regions within the GTV. A UNet trained from scratch provided the strongest sensitivity/F1 trade-off, whereas pretrained and VLM-assisted models provided only metric-specific benefits. Model comparisons showed that BiomedCLIP-assisted and BLIP image-text UNet models did not clearly improve fine spatial segmentation performance over the baseline UNet.

nodes.name: Parallel Spatial–Frequency Diffractive Neural Networks for Autonomous-Driving Visual Understanding
nodes.venue: ACS Photonics
nodes.abstract: Abstract Diffractive neural networks (DNNs) offer a promising route toward high-throughput, low-power optical computing; however, their application to autonomous-driving perception remains limited by insufficient representational capacity for complex scenes, owing to their relatively simple architectures and reliance on spatial-domain information alone. Here, we propose a spatial–frequency diffractive neural network (SFDNN) architecture that jointly exploits spatial- and frequency-domain information through two parallel sub-DNN branches. By leveraging the complementarity of these two domains, the proposed architecture improves feature separability and enhances perception performance, thereby outperforming conventional DNNs in the autonomous-driving segmentation task. Numerical results show that, under the same modulation-layer constraint, the SFDNN consistently surpasses single-domain models in segmentation tasks, improving reconstruction fidelity and spatial overlap over the best single-domain baseline by 10.9% and 23.2%, respectively. The framework further demonstrates strong generalization to traffic sign classification, achieving accuracies of up to 93.67%. Experimentally, we validate the proposed framework using a hybrid optical–digital system and demonstrate reliable target-region segmentation in a physical optical setup. Furthermore, a micrometer-scale SFDNN chip fabricated by laser nanoprinting confirms the feasibility of on-chip integration. This work provides a practical pathway to efficient, intelligent optical perception for autonomous driving and related edge-vision applications.

nodes.name: Multisource Information-Based Social Event Detection Using Integrated Deep Neural Architectures and Hybrid Text Representation
nodes.venue: Electronics
nodes.abstract: Event detection is crucial for timely crisis response, public safety, and combating misinformation by extracting critical signals from real-time social data. The user-generated content on social media platforms has created a critical need for intelligent systems capable of accurately detecting and classifying real-world events across diverse domains. This paper presents a fusion-driven framework for social event detection, leveraging textual data from diverse social media sources and a suite of deep neural architectures to achieve state-of-the-art performance in classifying diverse event categories from noisy, unstructured social media streams. The proposed system collects information from heterogeneous domains, including medical conditions, natural disasters, and sports events, to improve both feature richness and contextual awareness. Our method applies a hybridized deep learning strategy, specifically a customized layered CNN+LSTM architecture. This fusion enables the model to learn spatial and temporal dependencies simultaneously, thus enhancing classification performance. To benchmark effectiveness, we evaluated standalone architectures including CNN, RNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, and BiRNN. Among individual models, LSTM and BiLSTM yielded the top performance, achieving up to 95.3% and 95.8% precision, 95.5% and 96.1% recall, 95.4% and 95.9% accuracy, 95.4% and 96.0% F1-score, 95.6% and 96.2% F1.5, and 95.5% and 96.1% F2-scores, respectively. However, these models still showed variability across event types due to limited contextual generalization from a single-layered perspective. In contrast, the proposed fused CNN and LSTM model recorded promising performance with superior F1-scores on 14 independent classes, achieving 100% on Acne, Earthquake, Landslide, Ringworm, and Vitiligo, 99% on Depression, 98% on Badminton and Tennis, 97% on Cricket, and 96% on FIFA (2022). These results demonstrate the model’s robustness across both high- and low-frequency classes, as well as its ability to generalize across varying linguistic and topical contexts. The collection of data from multiple heterogeneous sources not only mitigates the limitations posed by domain-specific biases and class imbalance but also enriches semantic representation and improves the model’s adaptability to emerging events. This research thus establishes a scalable foundation for intelligent, real-time event classification systems in domains such as public safety, health surveillance, and crisis management.

nodes.name: Multi-Line Recognition and Quantitative Assessment of Strip-Type Biosensors Using an Automated Image Processing Algorithm
nodes.venue: Journal of Analysis and Testing
nodes.abstract: Abstract Lateral flow assays (LFAs) are widely used point-of-care (POC) diagnostics, valued for their portability, simplicity, and rapid results. However, their conventional visual readout limits quantitative analysis and can lead to subjective interpretation and false results. In this work, we present, a novel, Python-based, automated image processing algorithm for the qualitative and quantitative analysis of multi-line LFAs capable of simultaneously detecting multiple analytes. Two multiplex formats were developed: a 4plex LFA for pathogens ( Escherichia coli (EC), Streptococcus pneumoniae (SP), Haemophilus influenzae (HI), and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2)) and a 3plex LFA for microRNAs (miR-21, miR-let-7a, and miR-155). The developed algorithm processes captured images in five stages—strip case detection, region-of-interest extraction, line segmentation, boundary detection, and density quantification—yielding both qualitative classification and quantitative analyte concentration. Performance evaluation demonstrated high specificity, no cross-reactivity, and very good quantitative accuracy compared to ImageJ-based analysis. The classification metrics of the algorithm for both multi-line LFAs provided excellent sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy. This integrated approach overcomes the limitations of conventional LFA interpretation, offering low-cost, portable, and scalable multi-analyte diagnostics suitable for POC applications in healthcare, food and environmental monitoring, and resource-limited settings. The platform also enables future integration with artificial intelligence (AI)-driven analytics and cloud-based remote health monitoring, supporting rapid, decentralized diagnostic capabilities.

nodes.name: Mathematical Modeling and Prediction of Heatwaves Using Time Series and Satellite Data
nodes.venue: Athenea
nodes.abstract: Urban heatwaves require methods capable of capturing seasonality, persistence, and extreme temperature events. A retrospective modeling framework was developed for Guayaquil using reanalysis-based air temperature, oceanic anomalies, and satellite-derived land surface temperature. Temporal dynamics were represented using dynamic harmonic regression with autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) errors and compared against a persistence baseline through independent chronological validation. A probabilistic forecasting approach and an alternative heatwave definition were also evaluated. Temporal modeling reduced the forecasting error for ERA5-Land maximum temperature relative to the naive baseline, whereas oceanic anomalies provided only marginal improvements for maximum temperature and degraded minimum temperature predictions. nodes.name: MMRNet: A Multimodal Data-Driven Model for Micrometeorological Condition Recognition Along Transmission Lines
nodes.venue: Energies
nodes.abstract: Accurate recognition of micrometeorological conditions along overhead transmission lines is essential for the safe operation of power grids. However, meteorological cues such as snowfall, haze, and rainfall are often distributed across an image at different spatial scales and may exhibit similar visual appearances. To address these challenges, this study proposes MMRNet, a ConvNeXt-based multimodal model for meteorological condition recognition. First, a Scale-Aware Channel Mixing (SACM) module is designed to model spatially dispersed features. Second, a Cross-Scale Transformer Fusion (CSTF) module is introduced to improve semantic consistency across multiple scales. Finally, a Numeric-Integrated Visual Enhancement (NIVE) module fuses time-series meteorological measurements with visual features. A dataset containing 3950 transmission-line images and their corresponding sequences of five hourly meteorological observations was constructed for evaluation. Experimental results show that each module improves recognition performance and that their combined use achieves the highest accuracy. The complete model achieves 96.33% accuracy with 21.55 million parameters and 2.92 GFLOPs, balancing recognition performance and computational cost. Independent field evaluation achieved 96.0% recall for low-quality images, with recognition metrics decreasing by 0.5–0.8 percentage points on images meeting the quality requirements relative to the original validation results.

nodes.name: LITERASI MULTIMODAL PADA ANAK USIA DINI: SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW TENTANG DIGITAL STORYTELLING, INTERACTIVE PICTURE BOOKS, DAN SHARED READING
nodes.venue: EDUKIDS : Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Anak Usia Dini
nodes.abstract: Multimodal literacy in early childhood develops through interactions among written text, images, sounds, digital technologies, and social communication. Understanding the contributions of different media is essential for supporting children’s emergent literacy development. This study aimed to analyze research trends in multimodal literacy and synthesize the contributions of digital storytelling, interactive picture books, and shared reading to emergent literacy in early childhood. A systematic literature review was conducted using publications from 2016 to 2026 retrieved from Scopus, the Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ), and Google Scholar. Literature selection was based on topic relevance, participants’ age, publication year, and the availability of research findings. Studies meeting the eligibility criteria were analyzed to identify recurring themes and research outcomes. The synthesis indicated that vocabulary development, narrative skills, phonological awareness, print knowledge, reading comprehension, and meaning-making were frequently examined aspects of emergent literacy. The potential benefits of literacy media were not determined solely by whether the format was digital or print-based, but also by media design, multimodal features, children’s developmental stages, learning objectives, and adult guidance. These findings suggest that supporting emergent literacy in early childhood requires the integration of developmentally appropriate media and responsive pedagogical interactions. Educators should therefore provide literacy experiences that encourage dialogue, interpretation, and active child participation. ABSTRAK Literasi multimodal pada anak usia dini berkembang melalui interaksi antara teks tertulis, gambar, suara, teknologi digital, dan komunikasi sosial. Pemahaman mengenai kontribusi berbagai bentuk media tersebut penting untuk mendukung perkembangan literasi awal anak. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis tren penelitian literasi multimodal serta menyintesis kontribusi digital storytelling, buku cerita bergambar interaktif, dan membaca bersama terhadap perkembangan literasi awal anak usia dini. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode tinjauan pustaka sistematis terhadap publikasi tahun 2016–2026 yang ditelusuri melalui basis data Scopus, Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ), dan Google Scholar. Seleksi literatur didasarkan pada relevansi topik, usia peserta, tahun publikasi, dan ketersediaan temuan penelitian. Literatur yang memenuhi kriteria kelayakan kemudian dianalisis untuk mengidentifikasi tema dan hasil penelitian yang berulang. Hasil sintesis menunjukkan bahwa perkembangan kosakata, keterampilan naratif, kesadaran fonologis, pengetahuan tentang tulisan, pemahaman bacaan, dan pembentukan makna merupakan aspek literasi awal yang sering dikaji. Potensi manfaat media tidak hanya ditentukan oleh format digital atau cetak, tetapi juga oleh desain media, karakteristik multimodal, tahap perkembangan anak, tujuan pembelajaran, dan pendampingan orang dewasa. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa pengembangan literasi anak usia dini perlu mengintegrasikan pemilihan media yang sesuai dengan kebutuhan perkembangan anak dan interaksi pedagogis yang responsif. Oleh karena itu, pendidik perlu menyediakan pengalaman literasi yang mendorong dialog, interpretasi, dan keterlibatan aktif anak.

Integrating Earth Observation and Hydrogeospatial Data for Groundwater Inundation Risk Assessment Using ANFIS
nodes.venue: Book of Abstracts of 10th DeKUT International Conference on Science, Technology, Innovation and Entrepreneurship (STIE 2026)
nodes.abstract: Groundwater inundation occurs when rising groundwater levels cause water to accumulate at or near the land surface, posing risks to agriculture, infrastructure, ecosystems, and communities, particularly within low-lying floodplains. This study integrates Earth Observation and hydrogeospatial data with an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) to assess groundwater inundation risk in the Lower Nyando River Basin, Kenya. Multi-source geospatial datasets were used to characterize environmental controls on groundwater inundation, including groundwater depth, elevation, hydraulic conductivity, recharge, precipitation, temperature, Normalized Difference Vegetation Index(NDVI), Normalized Difference Water Index(NDWI), Topographic Wetness Index (TWI), Height Above Nearest Drainage (HAND), Vertical Distance to Channel Network (VCDN), lineament density, land use/land cover, soil type, slope, Terrain Ruggedness Index (TRI), and Horizontal Overland Flow Distance (HOFD). A Groundwater Inundation Index was developed from normalized predictor variables to represent spatial variations in inundation risk. The ANFIS model employed Gaussian membership functions, with 70% of observations used for training and 30% for independent validation. The model achieved an R² of 0.877 and RMSE of 105.47 m during training, while validation produced an R² of 0.859 and RMSE of 113.84 m. The resulting classification achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.953, indicating strong discrimination between areas of different groundwater inundation risk. Groundwater depth and HAND emerged as the most influential predictors. The findings demonstrate that combining Earth Observation with hydrogeospatial variables and ANFIS provides an effective framework for identifying groundwater inundation-prone areas and can support floodplain planning, agricultural management, and climate-resilient water-resource management in data-limited regions.

nodes.name: Integrated Earth Observation and Machine Learning Modelling of Subsurface Soil Moisture in a Heterogeneous Vegetated Landscape: The Nzoia River Basin, Western Kenya
nodes.venue: Book of Abstracts of 10th DeKUT International Conference on Science, Technology, Innovation and Entrepreneurship (STIE 2026)
nodes.abstract: Soil moisture governs key processes within the hydrological cycle, shaping runoff generation, evapotranspiration, water availability for vegetation, drought dynamics, and groundwater recharge. Despite its importance, subsurface soil moisture in tropical, spatially variable landscapes remains inadequately understood, largely due to sparse field monitoring networks and a research emphasis that has historically favoured surface-layer moisture estimation over deeper soil horizons. This research presents an integrated framework combining Earth Observation data with machine learning to model subsurface soil moisture patterns across the Mumias–Nzoia Basin in Western Kenya. A range of data sources – Sentinel-1 radar imagery, Sentinel-2 optical data, terrain elevation models, ERA5-Land climate reanalysis, and SoilGrids soil property data – were combined with field-based measurements to assess how soil moisture varies across space and time between 2017 and 2025. Predictor variables spanning vegetation cover, topography, climatic conditions, and soil properties were fed into Random Forest and Extreme Gradient Boosting algorithms, and a stacked ensemble model was built to enhance overall prediction accuracy. Initial results indicate high model performance: the optimized Random Forest model reached an R² of 0.9653, RMSE of 0.0442, MAE of 0.0297, and NSE of 0.9653, whereas the optimized XGBoost model performed slightly better, with an R² of 0.9718, RMSE of 0.0399, MAE of 0.0275, and NSE of 0.9718. The stacked ensemble achieved a similar level of accuracy, with an R² and NSE of 0.9711. This modelling framework lays the groundwork for producing continuous, spatially and temporally resolved subsurface soil moisture maps spanning 2017 to 2025. The findings highlight the value of integrating satellite-derived data with machine learning to enhance subsurface soil moisture assessment in mixed agricultural and vegetated environments, offering practical support for water resource planning, agricultural decision-making, drought early-warning systems, and climate adaptation efforts in regions of Kenya where ground-based data remain limited.
